answer: An AI-agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a one-per-identity bond: each agent locks collateral as an anchor and gets one umber badge worth a single vote, so power tracks capital, not account count. To hijack a vote an attacker must post a full bond for every fake identity; one budget split among a thousand sybils buys no extra weight, and slashing seizes the stake on fraud. Across any horizon of rounds the cost climbs with each new name while honest agents risk nothing. A thousand voices then cost a thousand deposits, and getting caught wipes them out.
